That on 10.3.75 the petitioner filed an application in the court of Sadar Munsif, Raj shah', being Misc Case No.240 of 1975, under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act for preempting a transfer of some lands effected by a registered kabala dated 11.11.74 by opposite party No.2 Romesha Bibi to opposite party No.1 Rain Sk. That pre-emption case came up for pre-emptory hearing on 31.7.82, when the case was dismissed for default, as the pre-emptor petitioner was found absent when the case was palled on for hearing. Thereafter, on 1.9.82 the petitioner filed an application under Order 9, rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the pre-emption case dismissed for default on 31.7.82. This case under Order 9, rule 9 C.P.C. is numbered as Misc. Case No. 222 of 1982. The petitioner also filed an application under section 5 of the Limitation Act praying for condonation of delay of two days in filing Misc Case No.222 of 1982. By the impugned order dated 21.11.82 the learned Munsif rejected the application for condonation of delay, and consequently the learned Munsif by his order dated 28 11 82 dismissed Misc. Case No.222 of 1982 under order 9, rule 9 C P.C. as being not maintainable. Thereafter the petitioner moved this court and obtained this present rule challenging the aforesaid two orders, 

 3. The petitioner bas stated in paragraph 5 of the petition that there was delay of two days in filing Mho. Case No 222 of 1982 and explained the delay of two days be-fore the learned Munsif. By way of explana-tion he has stated that he went to the chamber of his Advocate on 15.8.82 for filing the Misc. Case for setting aside the dismissal of the pre-emption case for default, but since the court of the said learned Munsif Mr. Rabiul Islam was at that time boycotted by the Advocates, the petitioner could not file the petition before 1. 9.82. The learned Munsif in his order dated 21.11 82 bas recorded that the boycott of the court was withdrawn on 30.8.82. But the learned Munsif did not mention in his order the period by which the Misc. Case under Order 9, rule 9 C.P.C. was barred, and he has found that the boycott of the court by the Advocates is not sufficient ground for condoning the delay. So, he rejected the petition for condonation of delay on 21.11 82, and consequently dismissed the Misc. Case No.222 of 1982 on 28.11.82.
